#' Price of a parcel
#'
#' Base rate plus rate per kilogram times chargeable weight, with the fuel surcharge of 12.5%,
#' the volume discount and the minimum price of 4.50.
#' @param zone destination zone: Local, National or Abroad
#' @param cw chargeable weight in kilograms
#' @param n number of parcels handed in at once
#' @export
parcel_price <- function(zone, cw, n = 1) {
  if (!zone %in% zone_rates$zone) stop("unknown zone")
  base <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "base_rate"]
  rate <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "rate_per_kg"]
  price <- base + rate * cw
  with_fuel <- price * (1 + 0.125)
  discounted <- with_fuel * (1 - volume_discount(n))
  round(pmax(discounted, 4.50), 2)
}

#' Volume discount
#'
#' Discount rate of 1% per parcel, capped at 20%.
#' @param n number of parcels handed in at once
#' @export
volume_discount <- function(n) {
  pmin(0.2, 0.01 * n)
}

#' Dimensional weight
#'
#' Weight derived from the volume of a parcel: \deqn{DW = \frac{L \cdot W \cdot H}{5000}}
#' @param l length in centimetres
#' @param w width in centimetres
#' @param h height in centimetres
#' @param divisor the fixed divisor, 5000
#' @export
dim_weight <- function(l, w, h, divisor = 5000) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(l), is.numeric(w), is.numeric(h))
  l * w * h / divisor
}

#' Chargeable weight
#'
#' The larger of actual weight and dimensional weight, never below 0.5 kilograms.
#' @param aw actual weight in kilograms
#' @param dw dimensional weight in kilograms
#' @export
chargeable_weight <- function(aw, dw) {
  cw <- pmax(aw, dw)
  pmax(cw, 0.5)
}

chunks_canon.text: This method sets out how the price of a parcel is determined from its size, its weight and its destination zone.
It applies to every parcel handed in at a counter. Pallets and letters are outside its scope.
The method is reviewed once a year by the pricing committee.
Actual weight (AW) is the weight of the parcel in kilograms as shown by the scale.
Dimensional weight (DW) is a weight derived from the volume of the parcel.
Chargeable weight (CW) is the weight on which the price is based.
The zone is the destination area of the parcel: Local, National or Abroad.
The dimensional weight is obtained from the length L, the width W and the height H of the parcel, measured in centimetres.
The divisor of 5000 is fixed and is not varied by zone.
The chargeable weight is the larger of the actual weight and the dimensional weight: CW = max(AW, DW).
The chargeable weight is never taken below 0.5 kilograms.
Weights are not rounded before the price is calculated.
Each zone has a base rate and a rate per kilogram, as set out in Table 1.

chunks_canon.caption: Table 1. Rates by zone
chunks_canon.text:
Zone; Base rate; Rate per kg
Local; 3.20; 0.85
National; 4.90; 1.10
Abroad; 9.50; 2.75
Rates are stated in the currency of the counter and exclude tax.
The price before surcharge is the base rate plus the rate per kilogram times the chargeable weight: P = B + R * CW.
B and R are taken from Table 1 for the zone of the parcel.
A fuel surcharge of 12.5% is added to the price before surcharge: S = P * (1 + 0.125).
The surcharge rate is set by the pricing committee and is the same for all zones.
A customer who hands in n parcels at once receives a discount rate of 1% per parcel, capped at 20%: D = min(0.2, 0.01 * n).
The discount is applied to the price after surcharge.

chunks_canon.caption: Figure 1. Discount rate by number of parcels
chunks_canon.text: Discount rate against number of parcels
The final price is never below 4.50, whatever the zone and the discount.
Final prices are rounded to 2 decimals.
Changes to Table 1 are approved by the pricing committee and recorded in the change log.
Questions about this method are answered by the pricing office.

#' Price of a parcel
#'
#' Base rate plus rate per kilogram times chargeable weight, with the fuel surcharge of 12.5%,
#' the volume discount and the minimum price of 4.50.
#' @param zone destination zone: Local, National or Abroad
#' @param cw chargeable weight in kilograms
#' @param n number of parcels handed in at once
#' @export
parcel_price <- function(zone, cw, n = 1) {
  if (!zone %in% zone_rates$zone) stop("unknown zone")
  base <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "base_rate"]
  rate <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "rate_per_kg"]
  price <- base + rate * cw
  with_fuel <- price * (1 + 0.125)
  discounted <- with_fuel * (1 - volume_discount(n))
  round(pmax(discounted, 4.50), 2)
}

#' Dimensional weight
#'
#' Weight derived from the volume of a parcel: \deqn{DW = \frac{L \cdot W \cdot H}{5000}}
#' @param l length in centimetres
#' @param w width in centimetres
#' @param h height in centimetres
#' @param divisor the fixed divisor, 5000

dim_weight <- function(l, w, h, divisor = 5000) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(l), is.numeric(w), is.numeric(h))
  l * w * h / divisor
}

chunks.text: This method sets out how the price of a parcel is determined from its size, its weight and its destination zone.
It applies to every parcel handed in at a counter. Pallets and letters are outside its scope.
The method is reviewed once a year by the pricing committee.
Actual weight (AW) is the weight of the parcel in kilograms as shown by the scale.
Dimensional weight (DW) is a weight derived from the volume of the parcel.
Chargeable weight (CW) is the weight on which the price is based.
The zone is the destination area of the parcel: Local, National or Abroad.
The dimensional weight is obtained from the length L, the width W and the height H of the parcel, measured in centimetres.
The divisor of 5000 is fixed and is not varied by zone.
The chargeable weight is the larger of the actual weight and the dimensional weight: CW = max(AW, DW).
The chargeable weight is never taken below 0.5 kilograms.
Weights are not rounded before the price is calculated.
Each zone has a base rate and a rate per kilogram, as set out in Table 1.

chunks.caption: Table 1. Rates by zone
chunks.text:
Zone; Base rate; Rate per kg
Local; 3.20; 0.85
National; 4.90; 1.10
Abroad; 9.50; 2.75
Rates are stated in the currency of the counter and exclude tax.
The price before surcharge is the base rate plus the rate per kilogram times the chargeable weight: P = B + R * CW.
B and R are taken from Table 1 for the zone of the parcel.
A fuel surcharge of 12.5% is added to the price before surcharge: S = P * (1 + 0.125).
The surcharge rate is set by the pricing committee and is the same for all zones.
A customer who hands in n parcels at once receives a discount rate of 1% per parcel, capped at 20%: D = min(0.2, 0.01 * n).
The discount is applied to the price after surcharge.

chunks.caption: Figure 1. Discount rate by number of parcels
chunks.text: Discount rate against number of parcels
The final price is never below 4.50, whatever the zone and the discount.
Final prices are rounded to 2 decimals.
Changes to Table 1 are approved by the pricing committee and recorded in the change log.
Questions about this method are answered by the pricing office.

units.text:
#' Price of a parcel
#'
#' Base rate plus rate per kilogram times chargeable weight, with the fuel surcharge of 12.5%,
#' the volume discount and the minimum price of 4.50.
#' @param zone destination zone: Local, National or Abroad
#' @param cw chargeable weight in kilograms
#' @param n number of parcels handed in at once
#' @export
parcel_price <- function(zone, cw, n = 1) {
  if (!zone %in% zone_rates$zone) stop("unknown zone")
  base <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "base_rate"]
  rate <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "rate_per_kg"]
  price <- base + rate * cw
  with_fuel <- price * (1 + 0.125)
  discounted <- with_fuel * (1 - volume_discount(n))
  round(pmax(discounted, 4.50), 2)
}

}

#' Dimensional weight
#'
#' Weight derived from the volume of a parcel: \deqn{DW = \frac{L \cdot W \cdot H}{5000}}
#' @param l length in centimetres
#' @param w width in centimetres
#' @param h height in centimetres
#' @param divisor the fixed divisor, 5000
#' @export
dim_weight <- function(l, w, h, divisor = 5000) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(l), is.numeric(w), is.numeric(h))
  l * w * h / divisor
}

#' Chargeable weight
#'
#' The larger of actual weight and dimensional weight, never below 0.5 kilograms.
#' @param aw actual weight in kilograms
#' @param dw dimensional weight in kilograms
#' @export
chargeable_weight <- function(aw, dw) {
  cw <- pmax(aw, dw)
  pmax(cw, 0.5)
}

#' Price of a parcel
#'
#' Base rate plus rate per kilogram times chargeable weight, with the fuel surcharge of 12.5%,
#' the volume discount and the minimum price of 4.50.
#' @param zone destination zone: Local, National or Abroad
#' @param cw chargeable weight in kilograms
#' @param n number of parcels handed in at once
#' @export
parcel_price <- function(zone, cw, n = 1) {
  if (!zone %in% zone_rates$zone) stop("unknown zone")
  base <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "base_rate"]
  rate <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "rate_per_kg"]
  price <- base + rate * cw
  with_fuel <- price * (1 + 0.125)
  discounted <- with_fuel * (1 - volume_discount(n))
  round(pmax(discounted, 4.50), 2)
}

parcel_price <- function(zone, cw, n = 1) {

#'

#' Dimensional weight
#'
#' Weight derived from the volume of a parcel: \deqn{DW = \frac{L \cdot W \cdot H}{5000}}
#' @param l length in centimetres
#' @param w width in centimetres
#' @param h height in centimetres

  l * w * h / divisor

#' Price of a parcel
#'
#' Base rate plus rate per kilogram times chargeable weight, with the fuel surcharge of 12.5%,
#' the volume discount and the minimum price of 4.50.
#' @param zone destination zone: Local, National or Abroad
#' @param cw chargeable weight in kilograms
#' @param n number of parcels handed in at once
#' @export
parcel_price <- function(zone, cw, n = 1) {
  if (!zone %in% zone_rates$zone) stop("unknown zone")
  base <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "base_rate"]
  rate <- zone_rates[zone_rates$zone == zone, "rate_per_kg"]
  price <- base + rate * cw
  with_fuel <- price * (1 + 0.125)
  discounted <- with_fuel * (1 - volume_discount(n))
  round(pmax(discounted, 4.50), 2)
}

#' Dose by body weight
#'
#' The body weight times the dose rate, never above 4000 milligrams.
#' @param weight body weight in kilograms
#' @param rate dose rate in milligrams per kilogram, defaults to 15
#' @export
dose_by_weight <- function(weight, rate = 15) {
  dose <- weight * rate
  pmin(dose, 4000)
}

#' Dose adjusted for kidney function
#'
#' The dose times the factor of the clearance band, rounded to 10 milligrams.
#' @param dose daily dose in milligrams
#' @param band clearance band: Normal, Reduced or Low
#' @export
adjusted_dose <- function(dose, band) {
  factor <- band_factors[band_factors$band == band, "factor"]
  round(dose * factor / 10) * 10
}

chunks_canon.text: This method sets out how the daily dose of the medicine is determined for an adult patient.
It applies to oral treatment only.
The body weight (W) is measured in kilograms, and the dose rate (R) is 15 milligrams per kilogram.
D = W * R
The daily dose is never above 4000 milligrams.
The dose is multiplied by the factor of the clearance band of the patient, as set out in Table 1.

The adjusted dose is rounded to 10 milligrams.

The function dose_by_weight multiplies the body weight by the dose rate of 15 milligrams per kilogram and never returns more than 4000 milligrams.
The function adjusted_dose multiplies the dose by the factor of the clearance band.

chunks.text: This method sets out how the daily dose of the medicine is determined for an adult patient.
It applies to oral treatment only.
The body weight (W) is measured in kilograms, and the dose rate (R) is 15 milligrams per kilogram.
D = W * R
The daily dose is never above 4000 milligrams.
The dose is multiplied by the factor of the clearance band of the patient, as set out in Table 1.

#' Dose by body weight
#'
#' The body weight times the dose rate, never above 4000 milligrams.
#' @param weight body weight in kilograms
#' @param rate dose rate in milligrams per kilogram, defaults to 15
#' @export

}

#'

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Risk-weighted amount
#'
#' The requirement scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.
#' @param k capital requirement per unit of exposure
#' @param ead exposure at default
#' @export
rwa <- function(k, ead) {
  k * 12.5 * ead
}

#' Effective maturity
#'
#' At least 1 year and capped at 5 years.
#' @param m maturity in years
#' @export
effective_maturity <- function(m) {
  pmin(pmax(m, 1), 5)
}

#' Asset correlation
#'
#' The asset correlation falls with the probability of default and lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @export
asset_correlation <- function(pd) {
  w <- (1 - exp(-50 * pd)) / (1 - exp(-50))
  0.12 * w + 0.24 * (1 - w)
}

#' Floor of the probability of default
#'
#' The probability of default is never taken below 0.03%.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param floor the floor, defaults to 0.0003
#' @export
floor_pd <- function(pd, floor = 0.0003) {
  pmax(pd, floor)
}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a + b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

chunks_canon.text: This methodology sets out how the capital requirement for unexpected losses is determined for each exposure.
It applies to all exposures of the lending book. Trading positions are outside its scope.
The probability of default (PD) is the likelihood that an obligor defaults within one year.
The loss given default (LGD) is the share of the exposure that is lost when the obligor defaults.
The exposure at default (EAD) is the amount outstanding when the obligor defaults.
The requirement uses the normal distribution function N and its inverse, where ρ denotes the asset correlation.

chunks_canon.caption: Table 1. Symbols

rows: capital requirement per unit of exposure

chunks_canon.text:
Symbol; Description
PDc; conditional probability of default
K; capital requirement per unit of exposure
M; effective maturity in years
The probability of default is estimated from internal ratings and is reviewed every year.
The probability of default is never taken below 0.03%.
The floor applies before any other step of the calculation.
The conditional probability of default is evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor.

equation.linear: pdc = normal_cdf((normal_inverse(pd) + sqrt(rho) * normal_inverse(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho))

chunks_canon.text: pdc = normal_cdf((normal_inverse(pd) + sqrt(rho) * normal_inverse(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho))
The confidence level of 0.999 is fixed and is set out again in Annex A.
The asset correlation falls with the probability of default: R = 0.12 * (1 - exp(-50 * PD)) / (1 - exp(-50)) + 0.24 * (1 - (1 - exp(-50 * PD)) / (1 - exp(-50))).
The correlation therefore lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
The loss given default is at least the floor of its segment, as set out in Table 3.

chunks_canon.caption: Table 3. Floors by segment
chunks_canon.text:
Segment; LGD floor
Retail; 0.15
Corporate; 0.25
Bank; 0.45
The unexpected loss rate is the conditional probability of default less the probability of default: UL = PDc - PD.
K is the product of LGD and UL.
Formula for the risk-weighted amount
The requirement is scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.
The effective maturity is at least 1 year.
The effective maturity is capped at 5 years.
This annex restates the fixed parameters of the methodology.
The confidence level is 0.999 for every segment.
Floors are reviewed once a year by the model owner.
The floor of the probability of default is 0.03%, as stated in section 3.1.1.
The floors of the loss given default are those of Table 3.

chunks_doc.text: This document describes how the package capreq implements the capital requirement methodology.
It is written for model validators and for the developers who maintain the package.
The function floor_pd applies the floor of 0.03% to the probability of default.
The function cond_pd evaluates the conditional probability of default at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor.

equation.linear: pdc = normal_cdf((normal_inverse(pd) + sqrt(rho) * normal_inverse(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho))

chunks_doc.text: pdc = normal_cdf((normal_inverse(pd) + sqrt(rho) * normal_inverse(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho))
The function asset_correlation returns a correlation between 0.12 and 0.24 that falls with the probability of default.
The floors of the loss given default are held in the object lgd_floors and are shown in Table D1.

chunks_doc.caption: Table D1. Floors by segment
chunks_doc.text:
Segment; LGD floor
Retail; 0.15
Corporate; 0.25
Bank; 0.45
The function capital_k multiplies the floored loss given default by the unexpected loss rate.
The function rwa scales the requirement by 12.5 and multiplies it by the exposure at default.
The function effective_maturity keeps the maturity between 1 year and 5 years.
The package is released after each yearly review of the methodology.

Capital requirement per unit of exposure
The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.

model_units.text:
#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

Risk-weighted amount
The requirement scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.

tags.text: capital requirement per unit of exposure

model_units.text:
#' Risk-weighted amount
#'
#' The requirement scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.
#' @param k capital requirement per unit of exposure
#' @param ead exposure at default
#' @export
rwa <- function(k, ead) {
  k * 12.5 * ead
}

#' Effective maturity
#'
#' At least 1 year and capped at 5 years.
#' @param m maturity in years
#' @export
effective_maturity <- function(m) {
  pmin(pmax(m, 1), 5)
}

#' Asset correlation
#'
#' The asset correlation falls with the probability of default and lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
#' @param pd probability of default

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default

  lgd_f * ul
}

chunks.text: This methodology sets out how the capital requirement for unexpected losses is determined for each exposure.
It applies to all exposures of the lending book. Trading positions are outside its scope.
The probability of default (PD) is the likelihood that an obligor defaults within one year.
The loss given default (LGD) is the share of the exposure that is lost when the obligor defaults.
The exposure at default (EAD) is the amount outstanding when the obligor defaults.
The requirement uses the normal distribution function N and its inverse, where ρ denotes the asset correlation.

units.text:
#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

units.text:
#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a + b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a + b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#' Asset correlation
#'
#' The asset correlation falls with the probability of default and lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @export
asset_correlation <- function(pd) {

}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a + b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default

  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Risk-weighted amount
#'
#' The requirement scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.
#' @param k capital requirement per unit of exposure
#' @param ead exposure at default
#' @export
rwa <- function(k, ead) {
  k * 12.5 * ead
}

#' Effective maturity
#'
#' At least 1 year and capped at 5 years.
#' @param m maturity in years
#' @export
effective_maturity <- function(m) {
  pmin(pmax(m, 1), 5)
}

#' Asset correlation
#'
#' The asset correlation falls with the probability of default and lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @export
asset_correlation <- function(pd) {
  w <- (1 - exp(-50 * pd)) / (1 - exp(-50))
  0.13 * w + 0.24 * (1 - w)
}

#' Floor of the probability of default
#'

#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param floor the floor, defaults to 0.0003
#' @export
floor_pd <- function(pd, floor = 0.0003) {
  pd
}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

chunks_canon.text: This methodology sets out how the capital requirement for unexpected losses is determined for each exposure.
It applies to all exposures of the lending book. Trading positions are outside its scope.
The probability of default (PD) is the likelihood that an obligor defaults within one year.
The loss given default (LGD) is the share of the exposure that is lost when the obligor defaults.
The exposure at default (EAD) is the amount outstanding when the obligor defaults.
The requirement uses the normal distribution function N and its inverse, where ρ denotes the asset correlation.

The probability of default is never taken below 0.03%.
The floor applies before any other step of the calculation.

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

model_units.text:
#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

You are given one piece of the model's R package - a function, a statement, a test, stored data or another file - exactly as written, followed, for context, by the pieces of the package it takes something from and the pieces that take something from it. Explain the one piece in the language of credit: the financial concept it implements (a probability of default, a loss given default, an exposure, a correlation, a capital requirement, a rating, a score, and so on); the inputs it takes and what each means financially; how it computes its result, as a formula an analyst would recognise; the parameters, floors, caps, thresholds and constants it fixes, and what they stand for; and what it returns and where that goes in the model. Say which methodological choices and assumptions the code makes, and where it follows or departs from a standard credit convention (the Basel formulas, for example), stated as fact, so that the analyst can set them against the methodology. Use the context only to understand this piece, and describe it only as far as it explains this one. Decide yourself how much detail the analyst needs: a sentence or two for a simple piece, as many paragraphs as an involved calculation deserves. Describe only what the code shows; where it relies on something the code does not show, say so, and do not guess. Do not rate, grade or recommend, and do not say whether the code is right: the analyst decides that. Write prose, with formulas in plain text where they help; no bullet points, headings or code blocks.

chunks.text: This methodology sets out how the capital requirement for unexpected losses is determined for each exposure.
It applies to all exposures of the lending book. Trading positions are outside its scope.
The probability of default (PD) is the likelihood that an obligor defaults within one year.
The loss given default (LGD) is the share of the exposure that is lost when the obligor defaults.
The exposure at default (EAD) is the amount outstanding when the obligor defaults.
The requirement uses the normal distribution function N and its inverse, where ρ denotes the asset correlation.

chunks.caption: Table 1. Symbols

rows: capital requirement per unit of exposure

chunks.text:
Symbol; Description
PDc; conditional probability of default
K; capital requirement per unit of exposure
M; effective maturity in years
The probability of default is estimated from internal ratings and is reviewed every year.
The probability of default is never taken below 0.03%.
The floor applies before any other step of the calculation.
The conditional probability of default is evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor.

equation.linear: pdc = normal_cdf((normal_inverse(pd) + sqrt(rho) * normal_inverse(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho))

chunks.text: pdc = normal_cdf((normal_inverse(pd) + sqrt(rho) * normal_inverse(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho))
The confidence level of 0.999 is fixed and is set out again in Annex A.
The asset correlation falls with the probability of default: R = 0.12 * (1 - exp(-50 * PD)) / (1 - exp(-50)) + 0.24 * (1 - (1 - exp(-50 * PD)) / (1 - exp(-50))).
The correlation therefore lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
The loss given default is at least the floor of its segment, as set out in Table 3.

The unexpected loss rate is the conditional probability of default less the probability of default: UL = PDc - PD.
K is the product of LGD and UL.
Formula for the risk-weighted amount
The requirement is scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.
The effective maturity is at least 1 year.
The effective maturity is capped at 5 years.
This annex restates the fixed parameters of the methodology.
The confidence level is 0.999 for every segment.
Floors are reviewed once a year by the model owner.
The floor of the probability of default is 0.03%, as stated in section 3.1.1.
The floors of the loss given default are those of Table 3.

units.text:
#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Risk-weighted amount
#'
#' The requirement scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.

}

#' Asset correlation
#'
#' The asset correlation falls with the probability of default and lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @export
asset_correlation <- function(pd) {
  w <- (1 - exp(-50 * pd)) / (1 - exp(-50))
  0.13 * w + 0.24 * (1 - w)
}

units.text:
#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}

#'

  lgd_f * ul

#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {

  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Loan period in days for an item class
#'
#' @param item_class one of "Standard", "Short" or "Reference"
#' @return the loan period in days
#' @export
loan_days <- function(item_class) {
  periods <- c(Standard = 14, Short = 2, Reference = 0)
  unname(periods[item_class])
}

#' Fine for an overdue item
#'
#' @param days_overdue whole number of days overdue
#' @param item_class one of "Standard", "Short" or "Reference"
#' @param daily_rate rate charged per day
#' @return the fine, capped at eight units
#' @export
fine_due <- function(days_overdue, item_class, daily_rate) {
  free <- if (item_class == "Standard") 2 else 0
  charged <- max(0, days_overdue - free)
  min(charged * daily_rate, 8)
}

#' Whether a loan may be renewed
#'
#' @param item_class one of "Standard", "Short" or "Reference"
#' @param renewals_so_far how many renewals have already been made
#' @param reserved whether another borrower has reserved the item
#' @export
may_renew <- function(item_class, renewals_so_far, reserved) {
  item_class == "Standard" && renewals_so_far < 2 && !reserved
}

#' Fine for an overdue item
#'
#' @param days_overdue whole number of days overdue
#' @param item_class one of "Standard", "Short" or "Reference"
#' @param daily_rate rate charged per day
#' @return the fine, capped at eight units
#' @export
fine_due <- function(days_overdue, item_class, daily_rate) {
  free <- if (item_class == "Standard") 2 else 0
  charged <- max(0, days_overdue - free)
  min(charged * daily_rate, 8)
}

Standard; 14; renewable twice no fine in the first two days
Short; 2; not renewable fine from the first day
Reference; 0; consulted on the premises only
Fines
The fine is the number of days overdue multiplied by the daily rate for the item class.
The fine for one item is capped at eight units.

Librarians may waive a fine; a waiver is recorded but does not change the calculation.
Renewals
A standard loan may be renewed twice, each renewal running for a further fourteen days.
A loan with a reservation against it may not be renewed.

#' Whether a loan may be renewed
#'
#' @param item_class one of "Standard", "Short" or "Reference"
#' @param renewals_so_far how many renewals have already been made
#' @param reserved whether another borrower has reserved the item
#' @export
may_renew <- function(item_class, renewals_so_far, reserved) {
  item_class == "Standard" && renewals_so_far < 2 && !reserved
}

#' Volume of water for one bed
#'
#' @param area_m2 the area of the bed in square metres
#' @param crop_group one of "leaf", "root" or "fruiting"
#' @return the volume in litres, capped at two hundred
#' @export
bed_volume <- function(area_m2, crop_group) {
  depths <- c(leaf = 4, root = 6, fruiting = 9)
  min(area_m2 * unname(depths[crop_group]), 200)
}

#' Whether a bed is watered on a given run
#'
#' @param moisture_pct the latest moisture reading, as a percentage
#' @param forecast_mm rain in the forecast, in millimetres
#' @param watered_today whether the bed has already been watered today
#' @export
water_bed <- function(moisture_pct, forecast_mm, watered_today) {
  !watered_today && moisture_pct <= 60 && forecast_mm <= 5
}

#' Volume of water for one bed
#'
#' @param area_m2 the area of the bed in square metres
#' @param crop_group one of "leaf", "root" or "fruiting"
#' @return the volume in litres, capped at two hundred

#' Whether a bed is watered on a given run
#'
#' @param moisture_pct the latest moisture reading, as a percentage
#' @param forecast_mm rain in the forecast, in millimetres

chunks.text: Irrigation field guide
Watering runs only between four and seven in the morning, when evaporation is lowest.
A bed is watered at most once a day. A second run on the same day is refused.
Where the forecast gives more than five 1 millimetres of rain, the run is skipped.
The volume for a bed is its area in square metres times the depth in millimetres set for its crop group.
The depth is four millimetres for leaf crops, six for root crops and nine for fruiting crops.
The volume for one bed is capped at two hundred litres in a single run.
A bed with a moisture reading above sixty per cent is skipped whatever the schedule says.
Where a sensor has not reported for two days its bed is watered on the schedule alone.
1 Rain is taken from the forecast issued at midnight, not from the gauge, because the run is planned before dawn.

#' Harbour rating
#'
#' The final rating of each harbour, from its factor scores, the factor weights, the adjustments
#' and the anchor rating.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours: throughput, berth_utilisation, liquidity_days
#' @param adjustments the names of the adjustments to apply
#' @return the facilities with their final rating
#' @export
harbour_rating <- function(facilities, adjustments = c("size", "governance")) {
  scored <- facilities %>%
    factor_scores() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(base_score = weighted_score(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score))
  adjusted <- adjust_score(scored, adjustments)
  anchored <- anchor_rating(adjusted)
  anchored %>% dplyr::mutate(final_rating = cap_rating(anchor, adjusted_score))
}

#' Factor scores
#'
#' Each factor scored from 1 (strongest) to 5 against its thresholds.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours
#' @export
factor_scores <- function(facilities) {
  limits <- utils::read.csv(system.file("extdata", "thresholds.csv", package = "harbourscore"))
  facilities %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      throughput_score = dplyr::case_when(throughput >= limits$high[1] ~ 1, throughput >= limits$low[1] ~ 3, TRUE ~ 5),
      utilisation_score = dplyr::case_when(berth_utilisation <= 0.6 ~ 1, berth_utilisation <= 0.85 ~ 3, TRUE ~ 5),
      liquidity_score = dplyr::if_else(liquidity_days >= 180, 1, 4))
}

#' Weighted score
#'
#' The factor scores weighted by the stored factor weights.
#' @param throughput_score score of the throughput
#' @param utilisation_score score of the berth utilisation
#' @param liquidity_score score of the liquidity
#' @export
weighted_score <- function(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score) {
  w <- factor_weights
  w$weight[w$factor == "throughput"] * throughput_score +
    w$weight[w$factor == "utilisation"] * utilisation_score +
    w$weight[w$factor == "liquidity"] * liquidity_score
}

#' Adjusted score
#'
#' The weighted score with the points of each adjustment added.
#' @param scored the scored facilities
#' @param adjustments the names of the adjustments to apply
#' @export
adjust_score <- function(scored, adjustments) {
  steps <- purrr::map_dbl(adjustments, function(name) adjustment_table$points[adjustment_table$adjustment == name])
  scored %>% dplyr::mutate(adjusted_score = base_score + sum(steps))
}

#' Anchor rating
#'
#' The adjusted score rounded to the half point, looked up in the anchor table.
#' @param adjusted the adjusted facilities
anchor_rating <- function(adjusted) {
  adjusted %>%
    dplyr::mutate(score_band = round(adjusted_score * 2) / 2) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(anchor_table, by = "score_band")
}

#' Capped rating
#'
#' A score above 4.5 takes the rating two notches below the anchor.
#' @param anchor the anchor rating
#' @param adjusted_score the adjusted score
cap_rating <- function(anchor, adjusted_score) {
  if (adjusted_score > 4.5) notch_down(anchor, 2) else anchor
}

#' Harbour rating
#'
#' The final rating of each harbour, from its factor scores, the factor weights, the adjustments
#' and the anchor rating.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours: throughput, berth_utilisation, liquidity_days
#' @param adjustments the names of the adjustments to apply
#' @return the facilities with their final rating
#' @export
harbour_rating <- function(facilities, adjustments = c("size", "governance")) {
  scored <- facilities %>%
    factor_scores() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(base_score = weighted_score(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score))
  adjusted <- adjust_score(scored, adjustments)
  anchored <- anchor_rating(adjusted)
  anchored %>% dplyr::mutate(final_rating = cap_rating(anchor, adjusted_score))
}

#' Factor scores
#'
#' Each factor scored from 1 (strongest) to 5 against its thresholds.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours
#' @export
factor_scores <- function(facilities) {
  limits <- utils::read.csv(system.file("extdata", "thresholds.csv", package = "harbourscore"))
  facilities %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      throughput_score = dplyr::case_when(throughput >= limits$high[1] ~ 1, throughput >= limits$low[1] ~ 3, TRUE ~ 5),
      utilisation_score = dplyr::case_when(berth_utilisation <= 0.6 ~ 1, berth_utilisation <= 0.85 ~ 3, TRUE ~ 5),
      liquidity_score = dplyr::if_else(liquidity_days >= 180, 1, 4))
}

#' Weighted score
#'
#' The factor scores weighted by the stored factor weights.
#' @param throughput_score score of the throughput
#' @param utilisation_score score of the berth utilisation
#' @param liquidity_score score of the liquidity
#' @export
weighted_score <- function(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score) {
  w <- factor_weights
  w$weight[w$factor == "throughput"] * throughput_score +
    w$weight[w$factor == "utilisation"] * utilisation_score +
    w$weight[w$factor == "liquidity"] * liquidity_score
}

#' Factor scores
#'
#' Each factor scored from 1 (strongest) to 5 against its thresholds.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours
#' @export
factor_scores <- function(facilities) {

    dplyr::mutate(

}

#' Harbour rating
#'
#' The final rating of each harbour, from its factor scores, the factor weights, the adjustments
#' and the anchor rating.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours: throughput, berth_utilisation, liquidity_days
#' @param adjustments the names of the adjustments to apply
#' @return the facilities with their final rating
#' @export
harbour_rating <- function(facilities, adjustments = c("size", "governance")) {
  scored <- facilities %>%
    factor_scores() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(base_score = weighted_score(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score))
  adjusted <- adjust_score(scored, adjustments)
  anchored <- anchor_rating(adjusted)
  anchored %>% dplyr::mutate(final_rating = cap_rating(anchor, adjusted_score))
}

chunks.text: Each harbour receives one rating from four factors, their weights, adjustments and an anchor.
The throughput is scored against the high and low thresholds: 1 at or above the high threshold, 3 at or above the low threshold, 5 below it.
The berth utilisation is scored 1 at or below 60%, 3 at or below 85%, and 5 above 85%.
The liquidity is scored 1 where the liquidity days are 180 or more, and 4 otherwise.
The weighted score is the sum of each factor score times its weight: throughput 40%, utilisation 35%, liquidity 25%.
The size and governance adjustments add their points to the weighted score, giving the adjusted score.
The adjusted score, rounded to the half point, is looked up in the anchor table to give the anchor rating.
An adjusted score above 4.5 takes the rating two notches below the anchor.
The rating is lowered by one notch when the throughput falls by more than 20% in the stress scenario.

chunks.text: harbour_rating gives each harbour its final rating. It scores the throughput, the berth utilisation and the liquidity with factor_scores, weights the scores with weighted_score, adds the adjustments with adjust_score, looks the adjusted score up in the anchor table and caps the rating two notches below the anchor above a score of 4.5.

The facilities data frame carries the throughput, the berth utilisation and the liquidity days of each harbour. The thresholds of the throughput are read from the file thresholds.csv; the weights, the adjustment points, the anchor table and the rating scale are stored data of the package.
The package also produces a quarterly dashboard of port congestion for the operations team.

units.text:
#' Harbour rating
#'
#' The final rating of each harbour, from its factor scores, the factor weights, the adjustments
#' and the anchor rating.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours: throughput, berth_utilisation, liquidity_days
#' @param adjustments the names of the adjustments to apply
#' @return the facilities with their final rating
#' @export
harbour_rating <- function(facilities, adjustments = c("size", "governance")) {
  scored <- facilities %>%
    factor_scores() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(base_score = weighted_score(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score))
  adjusted <- adjust_score(scored, adjustments)
  anchored <- anchor_rating(adjusted)
  anchored %>% dplyr::mutate(final_rating = cap_rating(anchor, adjusted_score))
}

units.text:
#' Factor scores
#'
#' Each factor scored from 1 (strongest) to 5 against its thresholds.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours
#' @export
factor_scores <- function(facilities) {
  limits <- utils::read.csv(system.file("extdata", "thresholds.csv", package = "harbourscore"))
  facilities %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      throughput_score = dplyr::case_when(throughput >= limits$high[1] ~ 1, throughput >= limits$low[1] ~ 3, TRUE ~ 5),
      utilisation_score = dplyr::case_when(berth_utilisation <= 0.6 ~ 1, berth_utilisation <= 0.85 ~ 3, TRUE ~ 5),
      liquidity_score = dplyr::if_else(liquidity_days >= 180, 1, 4))
}

units.text:
#' Weighted score
#'
#' The factor scores weighted by the stored factor weights.
#' @param throughput_score score of the throughput
#' @param utilisation_score score of the berth utilisation
#' @param liquidity_score score of the liquidity
#' @export
weighted_score <- function(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score) {
  w <- factor_weights
  w$weight[w$factor == "throughput"] * throughput_score +
    w$weight[w$factor == "utilisation"] * utilisation_score +
    w$weight[w$factor == "liquidity"] * liquidity_score
}

#' Adjusted score
#'
#' The weighted score with the points of each adjustment added.
#' @param scored the scored facilities

adjust_score <- function(scored, adjustments) {
  steps <- purrr::map_dbl(adjustments, function(name) adjustment_table$points[adjustment_table$adjustment == name])
  scored %>% dplyr::mutate(adjusted_score = base_score + sum(steps))
}

  adjusted %>%

    dplyr::left_join(anchor_table, by = "score_band")
}

}

#' Factor scores
#'
#' Each factor scored from 1 (strongest) to 5 against its thresholds.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours
#' @export
factor_scores <- function(facilities) {

    dplyr::mutate(
      throughput_score = dplyr::case_when(throughput >= limits$high[1] ~ 1, throughput >= limits$low[1] ~ 3, TRUE ~ 5),

      liquidity_score = dplyr::if_else(liquidity_days >= 180, 1, 4))
}

#' Harbour rating
#'
#' The final rating of each harbour, from its factor scores, the factor weights, the adjustments
#' and the anchor rating.
#' @param facilities a data frame of harbours: throughput, berth_utilisation, liquidity_days
#' @param adjustments the names of the adjustments to apply
#' @return the facilities with their final rating
#' @export
harbour_rating <- function(facilities, adjustments = c("size", "governance")) {
  scored <- facilities %>%
    factor_scores() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(base_score = weighted_score(throughput_score, utilisation_score, liquidity_score))
  adjusted <- adjust_score(scored, adjustments)
  anchored <- anchor_rating(adjusted)
  anchored %>% dplyr::mutate(final_rating = cap_rating(anchor, adjusted_score))
}
